texts.orig: 1. Project Overview
texts.text: 1. Project Overview

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Campus Library Assistant is a fictional information system designed to help university students find books, reserve study rooms, and understand library policies. This document is intentionally structured with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and cross-references so it can be used to test document parsing, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, and answer generation.
texts.text: Campus Library Assistant is a fictional information system designed to help university students find books, reserve study rooms, and understand library policies. This document is intentionally structured with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and cross-references so it can be used to test document parsing, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, and answer generation.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The system serves three campus libraries: Main Library, Engineering Library, and Medical Library. The Main Library is the only branch that operates 24 hours during examination weeks. The other branches keep their regular schedules during examination weeks.
texts.text: The system serves three campus libraries: Main Library, Engineering Library, and Medical Library. The Main Library is the only branch that operates 24 hours during examination weeks. The other branches keep their regular schedules during examination weeks.

texts.orig: 2. Library Opening Hours
texts.text: 2. Library Opening Hours

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Regular opening hours are shown below. Times use the local campus time zone. A closing time of 20:00 means the library closes at eight o'clock in the evening.
texts.text: Regular opening hours are shown below. Times use the local campus time zone. A closing time of 20:00 means the library closes at eight o'clock in the evening.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the official examination period, the Main Library extends its service to 24 hours every day. This special schedule does not apply to the Engineering Library or the Medical Library. The library website displays emergency closures separately from regular opening hours.

texts.orig: 3. Membership and Borrowing Rules
texts.text: 3. Membership and Borrowing Rules

texts.label: text
texts.orig: All currently enrolled students may borrow up to five books at a time. Faculty members may borrow up to ten books. Visiting researchers may use reading rooms but cannot borrow books unless they receive a temporary borrowing permit from the Library Director.
texts.text: All currently enrolled students may borrow up to five books at a time. Faculty members may borrow up to ten books. Visiting researchers may use reading rooms but cannot borrow books unless they receive a temporary borrowing permit from the Library Director.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A renewal is allowed only if no other member has placed a reservation on the book. Renewals must be submitted before the current due date. A book that is overdue cannot be renewed online; the member must contact the circulation desk.

texts.orig: 4. Study Room Reservations
texts.text: 4. Study Room Reservations

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Students can reserve group study rooms through the library portal. A reservation must be made at least 30 minutes before the requested start time and no more than seven days in advance. Each reservation lasts between 30 and 120 minutes.
texts.text: Students can reserve group study rooms through the library portal. A reservation must be made at least 30 minutes before the requested start time and no more than seven days in advance. Each reservation lasts between 30 and 120 minutes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A group study room requires at least two students and can hold up to six students. The person who creates the reservation is the booking owner and is responsible for checking in. Check-in opens 10 minutes before the reservation and closes 15 minutes after its start time.
texts.text: A group study room requires at least two students and can hold up to six students. The person who creates the reservation is the booking owner and is responsible for checking in. Check-in opens 10 minutes before the reservation and closes 15 minutes after its start time.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If the booking owner does not check in within the allowed period, the reservation is automatically cancelled and the room becomes available to other students. A student may hold only one future group-room reservation at a time.
texts.text: If the booking owner does not check in within the allowed period, the reservation is automatically cancelled and the room becomes available to other students. A student may hold only one future group-room reservation at a time.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5. Late Returns and Fines
texts.text: 5. Late Returns and Fines

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The standard overdue fine is 2 credits per book for each calendar day after the due date. The fine is capped at 40 credits per book. Friday and public holidays count as calendar days. A book returned on its due date has no overdue fine, even if it is returned after the library's normal closing time using the external return box.
texts.text: The standard overdue fine is 2 credits per book for each calendar day after the due date. The fine is capped at 40 credits per book. Friday and public holidays count as calendar days. A book returned on its due date has no overdue fine, even if it is returned after the library's normal closing time using the external return box.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Example: A student returns a book three calendar days after its due date. The fine is 6 credits. If the book is returned 30 days late, the uncapped fine would be 60 credits, but the student pays the maximum of 40 credits.
texts.text: Example: A student returns a book three calendar days after its due date. The fine is 6 credits. If the book is returned 30 days late, the uncapped fine would be 60 credits, but the student pays the maximum of 40 credits.

texts.orig: 6. Digital Services and Support
texts.text: 6. Digital Services and Support

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The library portal provides catalogue search, account status, room reservations, and renewal requests. It does not support payment of fines. Fine payments must be made at the Finance Office or through the university payment gateway.
texts.text: The library portal provides catalogue search, account status, room reservations, and renewal requests. It does not support payment of fines. Fine payments must be made at the Finance Office or through the university payment gateway.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For account or portal problems, contact library.support@example.edu. The support team responds Sunday through Thursday, 09:00-16:00. For urgent building-safety issues, contact Campus Security rather than the library support email.
